blockchain-ml.title: Blockchain-Enhanced Machine Learning
blockchain-ml.hook: A blockchain can make ML auditable. It cannot make it scale.
blockchain-ml.post:
Blockchains do not make machine learning automatically better.

In the prototypes I reviewed, accuracy improved as more parties joined, while throughput fell. Privacy noise bought privacy at an accuracy cost.

The useful question is not whether blockchain and ML can be combined. It is which trade-off the ledger actually buys.

cyber-events.title: Detecting Cyber Events in Turkish Streams
cyber-events.hook: The seven false positives matter as much as the 22 detections.
cyber-events.post:
29 alerts. 22 real events. Seven false positives.

That is the result I trust more than a rounded accuracy claim. The detector had to find rare cyber events in Turkish text, where preprocessing and entity history were core parts of the method.

A useful detector publishes what it gets wrong.

determinism.title: Why the Mean Is the Wrong Real-Time Metric
determinism.hook: 99.9% reliable still means 864 bad frames in four hours.
determinism.post:
99.9% sounds reliable. Over a four-hour, 60 Hz simulator session, it still permits 864 bad frames.

That is why mean frame time cannot demonstrate deadline compliance. The tail beyond the deadline matters, frame by frame.

Reliability percentages become meaningful only after you translate them into the failures a user will actually experience.

gradient-pinball.title: Gradient Descent, Momentum, and Failure
gradient-pinball.hook: A larger step can move faster and still take you nowhere.
gradient-pinball.post:
A larger gradient step can move faster and still take you nowhere.

Too much step size overshoots the valley. Momentum changes the geometry: sideways oscillations cancel while progress along the ravine accumulates.

The animation makes the stability problem visible before writing down the equation.

universal-jira.title: Can a Price Coordinate Software Agents?
universal-jira.hook: What if nobody assigned the work, and a price did?
universal-jira.post:
What if nobody assigned software work, and a price did?

An automated market maker can quote binary outcome prices that can be read as implied probabilities under defined payouts. That lets people or agents act on one public signal without waiting for a central coordinator.

This is an open research direction, not a published mechanism. Pricing coordinates action; verification still has to decide what was done.

oracles.title: How Can a Contract Verify an AI Verdict?
oracles.hook: The contract cannot run the model. Should it trust the answer?
oracles.post:
An AI returns a verdict. A smart contract cannot run the model or inspect its weights. Should it act?

A zero-knowledge proof can bind a committed model and input to an output without repeating the full inference on-chain. It proves the encoded computation, not that the model or input reflects reality.

That distinction is the trust boundary.

training-fingerprint.title: Proof-of-Learning and SecurePoL
training-fingerprint.hook: A model can be copied in seconds. Can it show how it learned?
training-fingerprint.post:
A trained model can be copied in seconds. The final weights contain no receipt for the compute that produced them.

Plain Proof-of-Learning aimed to make forgery cost at least as much as honest training, but later attacks found cheaper routes. SecurePoL adds a second constraint: the trajectory and a watermark-consistent ownership signal must agree.

Security here is a measured cost asymmetry, not an impossibility claim.

block-race.title: What Six Bitcoin Confirmations Really Buy
block-race.hook: Tripling the attacker raises risk about 544 times.
block-race.post:
Tripling an attacker's hashrate from 10% to 30% raises the six-confirmation catch-up risk from about 0.024% to 13.2%. That is roughly 544 times, not three.

Confirmations do not create certainty. They price the cost of rewriting history in energy and time.

redundancy-reactor.title: Why Identical Backups Fail Together
redundancy-reactor.hook: Two inertial systems failed. One software assumption defeated both.
redundancy-reactor.post:
Ariane 5 had two inertial reference systems running identical software. The backup failed first; the active unit stopped in the next 72 millisecond data cycle for the same reason.

Redundancy can protect against independent faults. Ariane 5 shows why duplicated hardware does not remove a common software failure.

The engineering lever is not only the number of backups. It is the independence of their failure paths.

watermarking-comparison.title: How Keyed LLM Text Watermarks Accumulate
watermarking-comparison.hook: A paragraph cannot prove authorship. It can carry a detectable watermark.
watermarking-comparison.post:
A paragraph cannot prove which model wrote it, but it can carry evidence of a keyed watermark.

A generative watermark uses prior context and a secret key to select a green list, then softly biases token choice toward it. No single word proves anything. The evidence accumulates across the passage as a measurable statistical deviation.

The 50% baseline in this film is an illustrative γ = 0.5 setting. The result is evidence at a chosen false-positive rate, not absolute authorship proof.

model-heist.title: Statistical Watermark Detection: A Teaching Model
model-heist.hook: Weak marks can add up. Only if the noise model is honest.
model-heist.post:
Weak coordinate-level marks can add up to strong aggregate evidence, but only under explicit assumptions.

In this Gaussian teaching model, a matched filter makes aligned signal add coherently while independent noise adds in quadrature. The result is a Z-test with an explicit threshold, false-positive rate and detection power.

This is statistical intuition, not the detector claimed by my 2024 paper. The distinction matters.
